parts.name: Jejunum
parts.info: The middle part of the small intestine, where most nutrients are absorbed through millions of tiny villi.
parts.fact: Thanks to its folds and villi, the inside of the small intestine has a surface of about 30 square metres.

parts.name: Ileum
parts.info: The last and longest part of the small intestine. It absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts.
parts.fact: It ends at the ileocaecal valve, which stops colon contents flowing back.

parts.name: Appendix
parts.info: A narrow, finger-like pouch hanging from the caecum. It holds lymphoid tissue and a reserve of gut bacteria.
parts.fact: Appendicitis is the most common reason for emergency abdominal surgery.

parts.name: Ascending colon & caecum
parts.info: Rises up the right side of the abdomen from the caecum, the pouch where the small intestine joins.
parts.fact: The caecum is where the colon's trillions of bacteria begin fermenting fibre.

parts.name: Transverse colon
parts.info: Crosses the upper abdomen from right to left, hanging below the stomach.
parts.fact: It is the most mobile part of the colon and can sag low in the abdomen.

parts.name: Descending & sigmoid colon
parts.info: Runs down the left side and curves into the S-shaped sigmoid colon. Water is absorbed and stool firms up here.
parts.fact: About 1.5 litres of fluid enters the colon each day, and all but about 100 ml is absorbed.

parts.name: Rectum
parts.info: The final 12–15 cm of the large intestine, which stores stool until it is passed.
parts.fact: Stretch sensors in its wall create the urge to go.

parts.name: Taeniae coli
parts.info: Three flat ribbons of muscle running along the colon. They are shorter than the colon, which bunches it into pouches (haustra).
parts.fact: All three taeniae meet at the base of the appendix, which helps surgeons find it.
